3. Pachytene: Tetrads, Recombination Nodules, & Crossing Over (Rad51/Dmc1 Recombinases)

quickSummary: Prophase I of Meiosis I consists of 5 sub-stages: 1) Leptotene (chromatin condenses into threads forming the bouquet stage), 2) Zygotene (homologous chromosomes undergo synapsis held by the tripartite Synaptonemal Complex to form bivalents), 3) Pachytene (crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids catalyzed by the Recombinase complex at recombination nodules), 4) Diplotene (synaptonemal complex dissolves, revealing X-shaped Chiasmata; oocytes arrest in dictyotene), and 5) Diakinesis (chiasmata undergo complete terminalization).

conceptBreakdown.content: Meiosis is a specialized double-division process in germ cells reducing the chromosomal complement from diploid ($2n$) to haploid ($n$), generating genetic diversity through independent assortment and crossing over.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Five Sequential Sub-Stages of Prophase I
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Five Sequential Sub-Stages of Prophase I
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PROPHASE I SUB-STAGE DYNAMICS
                      
   1. LEPTOTENE ─────► Chromatin condenses into long threads; telomeres attach
                       to inner nuclear envelope forming a **Bouquet Stage**.
                       
   2. ZYGOTENE ──────► Homologous chromosomes pair up (**SYNAPSIS**) forming
                       **Bivalents**. Paired axes held by the **Synaptonemal Complex**.
                       
   3. PACHYTENE ─────► Bivalents appear clearly as **Tetrads** (4 chromatids).
                       **CROSSING OVER** occurs between non-sister chromatids,
                       catalyzed by the **Recombinase Complex** at **Recombination Nodules**.
                       
   4. DIPLOTENE ─────► Dissolution of Synaptonemal Complex; homologous chromosomes
                       separate EXCEPT at X-shaped crossover points called **CHIASMATA**.
                       *(Arrests in human oocytes as Dictyotene stage)*.
                       
   5. DIAKINESIS ────► **TERMINALIZATION OF CHIASMATA** (chiasmata shift to ends);
                       nucleolus & nuclear envelope disappear; spindle forms.
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Synaptonemal Complex (SC)**: A tripartite proteinaceous ladder-like scaffold (2 lateral elements + 1 central element linked by transverse filaments) that aligns homologous chromosomes gene-for-gene during Zygotene.
• **Crossing Over**: Enzymatic exchange of genetic material between **non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes** mediated by **Recombination Nodules (Rad51 / Dmc1 recombinases)** during Pachytene.
• **Dictyotene Arrest**: Female mammalian primary oocytes arrest in Diplotene of Prophase I during fetal development, resuming division only at ovulation.
